chapter: Next Time, On King of Invokations...
act_title: Next Time, On King of Invokations...

quests.title: Next Time, On King of Invokations...

dialogue.t: *sigh* I want to go back to Inazuma... How could this happen to me...
Traveler? *sigh* Don't even mention the novel. Those researchers working on Genius Invokation TCG are barely holding it together.
According to a researcher I know quite well, the team encountered all kinds of problems that could only be described as baffling...
For example, a Haravatat researcher suddenly asked a question one day.
He said that if the effect descriptions on the cards are too long, it might discourage people who aren't used to reading long blocks of text from playing the game.
Researchers are used to reading large chunks of text and aren't affected by this issue, but the long descriptions could very well turn potential players away.
So he suggested cutting the amount of text on some cards in half to make them easier to read.
It's not a problem to me... But the researchers are still working hard on this issue. After all, it's about the player's experience, and the fewer problems, the better.
Anyway... There's an even bigger problem. They promised to help me find models for my novel, but something went wrong with that, too.
Remember? I told you earlier about a researcher who said they'd introduce me to Tighnari and Cyno, and ask them to be the inspirations for my novel.
But they're so busy. I don't think I can count on them for a while...

dialogue.sit: How will you get in touch?

dialogue.t: The researcher who received me was not able to help me with this, but he gave me an idea.
He said Cyno sometimes goes to Puspa Café to play cards.
If I want... I can try my luck there first. Or maybe they'll help me get in touch when they're free.
*sigh* By the time they're free, I'll have finished writing the novel.
I guess I'll go myself and see if I can find Cyno.
But if I'm lucky enough to meet Cyno at the café, how should I even introduce myself to him? What a dilemma...
Really!? That's amazing! But how did you... Uh, you know what? I'm not gonna pry further.
What are we waiting for then? Let's head to Puspa Café right now! Hope we'll be able to catch Cyno...
Shh... I—Isn't that Cyno?
Look at his outfit, his hairstyle, and that hair color... This is exactly what a protagonist in a card game novel should look like!

dialogue.sit: This has no rhyme nor reason...
I actually know quite a lot of people who can fit into this category...

dialogue.t: Heh, just trust my instincts on the market. But now's not a good time to explain...
Traveler, please ask Cyno to be the model for my novel... I'm counting on you!
...Hmm, this combination of cards isn't so bad.
But they're not strong enough to deal with quick attacks...

dialogue.sit: What are you up to, Cyno?

dialogue.t: {NICKNAME}? I didn't expect to see you here.
I'm in the middle of trying to build a Genius Invokation deck with a relatively slow attack speed.
I'm hoping that the deck would allow the player to obtain an abundance of resources and plenty of powerful cards...
But to be honest, it's hard to build a deck like that...
Currently, in the Genius Invokation TCG community, some players prefer to use cards with fast attack speeds.
At the beginning of the game, they play a large number of cards in one go in order to swiftly defeat their opponent.
But I'm no fan of this tactic. I prefer to continuously accumulate resources in different ways...
Seizing every possible opportunity, building up my advantage, and eventually securing the victory...
Yes, yes! Wonderful! You're just like the main character in my novel!
Sorry! Uh... I'm...

dialogue.sit: This is the author of "King of Invokations."

dialogue.t: Hello, General Mahamatra. I don't suppose you've heard of me...
I've read your novel. It's very good.
I'm truly honored!

In the novel, every time the protagonist is at a disadvantage, he always manages to get a card that wasn't in his deck through various means, then defeats his opponent. This left a lasting impression on me.
I understand that writing novels requires taking a creative license, but this way of winning is a departure from the fundamental mechanics of Genius Invokation TCG.

About that, well... Although I do play Genius Invokation TCG a lot, I'm not really good at it... And if you write about the duels with a competitive mindset, it wouldn't make for an interesting story.
Hmm, is that so? Well, as luck would have it, I've just built two decks of cards, so we can play a few rounds of Genius Invokation TCG here. Maybe you'll find some inspiration.

dialogue.sit: (Now they are about to play cards...)
(This guy simply wants to play cards...)

dialogue.t: Eh? Playing with... with you? I'd love to, but the truth is...

dialogue.sit: You take several pictures of Cyno very quickly...

dialogue.t: This has been a big help. I'm sure Asagiri will make an excellent illustration!
Thank you very much, Cyno. I'll be sure to send you a copy of the novel as soon as it's published.
Uh, Cyno, the two decks you're holding are...?
Didn't you promise to play a few games of Genius Invokation TCG with me earlier?
Eh!? I—I'm not very good at it, so uh... Traveler! You're definitely better than me!
Then the matter is settled. Here, take this quick attack deck.
I'm going to use this relatively slower deck to see how I can deal with your attacks.
I'll do my best, Cyno...
Cyno, your play style is so... slow and deliberate...
It's just an intuitive strategy.

quests.description: Something seems to be bothering the novelist, Fukumoto…
